items.title: Marty Sheller interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 9, 2022
items.q: Frankie Malabé ... was the one who took me down that road of starting me off listening to Tito Puente and Tito Rodriguez and Machito

ctx.x: That’s not unusual. That’s a common thing for people who are not raised in that culture and are used to hearing it all the time, the same way somebody in a Latin community would listen to a blues and not know where does it start? Well you know where it starts because you can hear where it starts. But they’re not used to hearing it that way. So that’s not an uncommon thing. Like I said, when I first started learning about it, boy that bass part really threw me off and I had the same question, where is the one? As…
Was your work as an arranger and music director subject to the whims of popular music over the years? Or was the Latin music community a more level playing field?
